tool.name: ampvis2 rarefaction curve
tool.description: generates a rarefaction curve (number of reads vs number of observed OTUs)
tool.command: Rscript -e ' library(ampvis2) data <- readRDS('${input_dataset}') # set up metadata meta <- data.frame() # loop through all metadata columns for (col in colnames($metadata)) { # add column to metadata dataframe meta[[col]] <- sapply(strsplit(colnames(data), "_"), "[[", $metadata[col]) } # write metadata to file write.table(meta, "meta.txt", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, sep = "\t") # run the rarecurve function res <- amp_rarecurve( data, samples = ${samples}, metadata = "meta.txt", facet_by = "${facet_by}", color_by = "${color_by}", nboot = ${nboot}, min_reads = ${min_reads}, max_reads = ${max_reads}, step = ${step} ) # save the result saveRDS(res, "output.rds") '

param.label: Samples to include in the analysis
Facet by
param.help: Split the plot into multiple panels based on the selected metadata variable.

param.label: Color by
param.help: Color the points based on the selected metadata variable.

param.label: Number of bootstrap replicates
param.help: Number of bootstrap replicates to perform for confidence intervals.

param.label: Minimum number of reads
param.help: Minimum number of reads per sample to consider.

param.label: Maximum number of reads
param.help: Maximum number of reads per sample to consider.

param.label: Step size
param.help: Step size for increasing the number of reads.

tool.help:
What it does ============
Generates a rarefaction curve (number of reads vs number of observed OTUs) for each sample. The plot can be colored or faceted (i.e. split into multiple panels) by metadata
The Galaxy tool calls the `amp_rarecurve <https://kasperskytte.github.io/ampvis2/reference/amp_rarecurve.html>`_ function of the ampvis2 package.
Input =====
An ampvis2 RDS dataset obtained by the ``ampvis2: load`` tool (or ``ampvis2: mergereplicates`` or one of the ``ampvis2: subset ...`` tools).
The metadata list output of the ``ampvis2: load`` tool (or ``ampvis2: mergereplicates`` or the ``ampvis2: subset sample`` tool). This input is only used for providing values to the parameters alowing to select metadata variables or values.
Output ======
Rarefaction curves in the chosen output format.
